arguments.value: Robert Gary Klausner (born 1941 in Los Angeles, California) is a United States District Judge for the Central District of California, appointed by President George W. Bush in 2002. He earned a B.A. from the University of Notre Dame in 1963, a B.S. from the University of Notre Dame in 1964, and a J.D. from Loyola Law School in Los Angeles in 1967. He served in the U.S. Army from 1967 to 1969, then worked as a deputy district attorney in Los Angeles County from 1969 to 1974. He subsequently served as commissioner and judge of the Pasadena Municipal Court from 1974 to 1985 and as a judge of the Superior Court of California, County of Los Angeles, from 1985 to 2002 before joining the federal bench.
